name: Rhizomorph system
description: Root-like organs with their own growing tip and a protective rind grow through soil or air without feeding, and persist for decades. The family is both parasite and saprotroph and infects roots on contact.

tip_speed.note: from the type species Armillaria gallica: rhizomorphs 146 to 308 um/h, from a search snippet; ordinary hyphae 63 um/h (research/01-growth-biology.md [25])

growth_unit.note: no measurement found; rhizomorphs branch rarely

branch_angle_sd.note: as for the type species Armillaria gallica: default from Hopkins & Boswell 2012 (79 +/- 10 deg, research/09); not measured for the type species

sensitivity.note: how strongly tips turn away from crowding; model coefficient

fusion_probability.note: chance a tip that meets a hypha fuses and does not cross; no measurement found

density_cap.note: hyphal density at which branching stops; tuning value

cord_max.note: largest rhizomorph cross-section, in single hyphae; tuning value

uptake_rate.note: tuning value, set to tip speed / segment length so that one feeding segment can supply about one growing tip; no measurement found

inactivation_rate.note: as for the type species Armillaria gallica: from Rhizoctonia solani (Boswell et al. 2003, research/09); not this species (0.5 per day)

degradation_rate.note: none seen in 15 h in R. solani; small value so dead hyphae clear

passive_transport.note: diffusion between neighbouring segments; measured diffusion inside hyphae (1 to 2 x 10^-9 m2/s, research/10) is several times faster than the passes allow

soil.note: how well it feeds on this substrate; from its ecology, not measured

wood.note: how well it feeds on this substrate; from its ecology, not measured

litter.note: how well it feeds on this substrate; from its ecology, not measured

root.note: how well it feeds on this substrate; from its ecology, not measured

agar.note: how well it feeds on this substrate; from its ecology, not measured

transport_speed.note: from the type species Armillaria gallica: more than 20 mm/h reported for Armillaria (research/09-boswell-check.md section 6 (Fricker et al. 2017))

cold_drop.note: fruits in autumn; size of the drop is a guess

wobble.note: tuning value for the 4K engine; not a measured quantity

avoidance.note: tuning value for the 4K engine; not a measured quantity

fusion_probability.note: tuning value for the 4K engine; not a measured quantity

uptake.note: tuning value for the 4K engine; not a measured quantity

turn.note: tuning value for the 4K engine; not a measured quantity

spike_interval.note: from the type species (as Armillaria bulbosa): spontaneous firing at 0.5 to 5 Hz, taken as 1 Hz (research/04 [14] via [25]). Intracellular microelectrode recording, reported second-hand: not comparable with the extracellular figures used for other families

spike_duration.note: from the type species: 20 to 500 ms, from a search summary (research/04 [14])

spike_amplitude.note: from the type species: 5 to 50 mV, intracellular (research/04 [14] via [25]); low confidence

score.note: placed just below the cord formers: Hypholoma fasciculare is reported (unchecked) to be used as a biocontrol against Armillaria (research/08), and combat rank rises with extension rate (research/06 [2][3]). No direct measurement
